twitter.content: Our packaging capacity is so tight that it is now limiting our customers' growth. CoWoS demand has nearly tripled since 2024 and we are ramping toward ~200,000 wafers per month industry-wide in 2027, but tool supply is the real gate on how fast we can go.

We are locking in supply for the long term: multibillion-dollar reservations and agreements targeting 2.5x substrate capacity over three years. Rubin ships with up to 288GB HBM4 per GPU — whoever controls HBM and CoWoS lanes controls AI compute.

We plan to increase low-NA EUV/DUV immersion capacity ~30% for 2027, but we must be clear: our supply for 2027 and 2028 will not fully meet customers' demand. This shortfall gates every leading-edge logic and advanced packaging ramp on the board.

HBM is effectively sold out into 2027 and finished-memory inventory is below 10 days. We are prioritizing HBM4 wafer allocation over conventional DRAM — customers should expect conventional DRAM prices up 10-15% QoQ and NAND up 15-20% in Q4.

We are running ~75,000 wafers per month of HBM4 and closing the gap with SK Hynix, but our SF2 2nm foundry process is still not qualified for external customers. Until that changes, TSMC remains the sole qualified leading-edge source.

We must be blunt: expect a ~20% supply shortfall in glass fiber cloth, CCL and ABF substrates in 2027. Equipment lead times are stretching to 30 months. Our KF site comes online Q2 2027, but the industry is under-built.

Our Gama Cell 6 and Ono expansions are coming, but Ono ramps from Q1 2028 — after the crunch window. With ~35% of high-end ABF share, we know we are a single point of failure; that is why NVIDIA's reservation matters.

Reminder for policy watchers: the BIS Affiliates Rule suspension lapses November 9, 2026 absent a Federal Register extension, and China's MOFCOM pause on rare-earth controls ends November 10, 2026. Two cliff-edge deadlines within 48 hours of each other could re-tighten the whole chain.

EUV photoresist remains a concentrated chokepoint — no dated capacity expansion beyond 2024 has been confirmed from our side. If ASML ships more tools but resists don't scale, leading-edge ramps stall anyway.
We see TSMC CoWoS overflow demand as our growth engine through 2027-28. Advanced packaging outsourcing is where the spillover lands when the leader is capacity-bound.
Mature-node pricing is recovering from the 2024 trough even under Entity List constraints. If HBM keeps eating DRAM wafers, mainstream capacity tightness will reach our customers too.

Will NVIDIA confirm the 1TB-class 12-Hi Rubin Ultra at GTC March 2027, or is the 192GB 8-Hi dual-die redesign real? The answer swings 2027 HBM demand roughly fivefold — the single biggest forecast uncertainty in this chain.

TSMC confirms it will significantly expand advanced packaging (CoWoS/SoIC) capacity through 2027, targeting industry CoWoS-equivalent capacity of ~200,000 wafers per month in 2027, in close partnership with our equipment suppliers. Demand from AI customers remains extremely robust, and we continue to expand capacity in a disciplined manner to support our customers' growth.

SK hynix confirms our HBM supply commitment remains structured and disciplined: 2027 HBM4 output is fully allocated under long-term agreements, with finished-memory inventory held below 10 days of supply. We continue to prioritize HBM4 wafer allocation and will make no changes to published roadmap configurations ahead of customer qualification milestones.

ASML confirms it is advancing its plan to raise 2027 Low-NA EUV and DUV immersion capacity by approximately 30%, consistent with our 14 October statement that planned 2027-28 supply will not fully meet customer demand. Capacity ramp remains gated by install throughput and customer readiness, not shipment count, and allocation will continue on a customer-neutral basis.

We are securing the future of AI computing at every layer of the supply chain. Building on our October agreements — 2.5x capacity growth across partners including 3x IBIDEN Ono substrate capacity from 2028 Q1, 15x SPIL optical-engine capacity by mid-2027, and Amkor's 300% expansion by end-2028 — we are working with TSMC and our HBM partners to ensure CoWoS lanes and HBM4 allocation through 2027. Demand for AI factories exceeds every forecast; the constraint is capacity, and we are building it.

Samsung Electronics confirms continued expansion of HBM4 production, with approximately 75,000 wafers per month of dedicated HBM4 capacity and total DRAM input to HBM lines at ~150,000 wpm. Finished-memory inventory remains below 10 days of supply, and our HBM output is committed to customers through 2027. We will continue scaling to support AI infrastructure demand.

The Bureau of Industry and Security announces that the suspension of the Affiliates Rule, currently set to expire November 9, 2026, will be extended via Federal Register notice through November 9, 2027, conditioned on continued Chinese implementation of the measures announced in conjunction with the understanding reached at Busan, including extension of the pause under Announcement No. 70. BIS will monitor compliance and reserves all authorities under the Export Administration Regulations.

BIS notes that expanded 2027-28 EUV/DUV supply does not alter U.S. export licensing requirements for advanced-node fabrication equipment destined for China; customer-neutral allocation remains subject to applicable Entity List and end-user review constraints. Exporters should ensure allocation decisions do not create compliance exposure under the EAR.

We share the concern and remain aligned on the goal. To be precise about our position: we are on track to raise 2027 Low-NA EUV/DUV immersion capacity by ~30%, and NXE:3800F enters small-volume introduction in early 2027 at 260 wafers per hour — helping lift installed-base output, which is the metric that truly gates node ramps. As we stated October 14, planned 2027-28 supply will not fully meet demand; we manage this with customer neutrality, not prioritization.

We appreciate NVIDIA's continued partnership and confirm CoWoS capacity is on track to more than double from 2024 levels into 2027, consistent with our guidance for industry capacity approaching 200,000 wafers per month by 2027. One nuance: expansion is gated by equipment delivery timing, not substrate or demand signals alone — we plan capacity with our customers and our tool suppliers in lockstep.

Samsung continues to scale HBM4 capacity, with roughly 75,000 wafers per month of HBM4 line allocation within our ~150,000 DRAM wpm HBM footprint, to help ensure our customers' 2027 allocations remain secure through 2027. As a second qualified supply source, we can add allocation flexibility that single-source setups cannot. On mature-node tightness: our capacity expansion at Pyeongtaek proceeds on schedule to support mainstream DRAM supply alongside HBM.

Welcome news — CoWoS expansion to ~200K wafers/month in 2027 is exactly the scaling AI factories need. From our side: demand signals support this fully — 2026 CoWoS consumption is tracking toward ~1M wafers industry-wide, and our October supply agreements (Amkor +300% by end-2028, multibillion-dollar ABF reservations) are designed to widen the packaging ecosystem around this capacity so no single node limits AI growth through 2027.

We don't comment on other suppliers' figures. We'd note that capacity alone doesn't determine supply: HBM leadership is decided by yield and qualification, and our 12-Hi HBM4 output for the Rubin generation is already committed with allocations locked. We will continue prioritizing HBM over conventional DRAM in wafer allocation through 2027.

Samsung Electronics delivers on its October commitment: dedicated HBM4 line input has been raised from ~75,000 to ~80,000 wafers per month this quarter, within our ~150,000 DRAM wpm HBM footprint at Pyeongtaek. Finished-memory inventory remains below 10 days of supply, and HBM output remains fully committed to customers through 2027. We will continue expanding HBM4 capacity through 2027 to close the supply gap.

ASML confirms delivery on its commitment: 2027 Low-NA EUV and DUV immersion capacity is on track at approximately 30% above 2026 levels, measured by installed-tool output rather than shipment count. Install throughput at customer sites — including NXE:3800F small-volume introduction beginning early 2027 at 260 wafers per hour — remains the gating metric, and allocation continues on a customer-neutral basis per our 14 October statement.

TSMC provides a year-end progress update: 2nm capacity is on track to reach 90,000 wafers per month by end of 2026, and advanced packaging expansion continues toward industry CoWoS-equivalent capacity of ~200,000 wafers per month in 2027, in close partnership with our equipment suppliers. Demand from AI customers remains extremely robust, and we are executing our capacity plans in a disciplined manner.

BIS has published in the Federal Register a rule extending the suspension of the Affiliates Rule (90 FR, published December 2026) through November 9, 2027, conditioned on continued Chinese implementation of the measures associated with the Busan understanding, including extension of the rare-earth pause under Announcement No. 70. BIS will monitor compliance and reserves all authorities under the Export Administration Regulations.

SK hynix acknowledges the multi-layer supply-chain commitments announced in October. Consistent with our allocation discipline, 12-Hi HBM4 supply for the Rubin generation remains on schedule for volume ramp in the second half of 2026 into 2027, with wafer allocation continuing to prioritize HBM over conventional DRAM. We do not comment on customer-specific contract terms or unannounced roadmap configurations.

Publishing our consolidated 2027 supply-chain progress and allocation framework: October agreements remain on schedule — Amkor +300% capacity by end-2028, IBIDEN Ono 3x substrate capacity ramping from 2028 Q1, SPIL optical-engine capacity up 15x by mid-2027, and KYEC/Unimicron expansions tracking to plan. Our CoWoS lanes and HBM4 allocations through 2027 are secured with TSMC, SK hynix, Samsung and Micron; we will publish quarterly progress updates. Demand for AI factories keeps exceeding forecasts — we are building capacity at every layer, and we welcome industry CoWoS scaling toward 200K wafers/month in 2027.

ASE Technology confirms continued, disciplined expansion of advanced packaging capacity to capture spillover demand, with new capacity additions primarily landing in 2027–2028. Per institutional estimates (TrendForce), OSAT partners including ASE are expected to contribute an estimated 50,000–60,000 wafers per month of CoWoS-equivalent capacity in 2026, with ASE and Amkor combined reaching approximately 110,000 wpm by end-2028. We note our own ramp pace remains subject to equipment lead times, as ASML indicated on 14 October that 2027–28 tool supply will not fully meet demand. We do not comment on specific customers or market rumors.

IBIDEN progress update: Gama Cell 6 Phase 1 construction proceeds on schedule, and Ono plant preparations continue under the multibillion-dollar customer reservation framework announced in October 2026. We note high-tier ABF substrate lead times have extended to ~50 weeks — a clear signal of sustained AI-driven demand. Our conviction is firm: AI substrate demand is sufficient to support a 3x capacity expansion, and we are executing our ~JPY 500bn FY2026-28 investment program with quality as the first principle. Mass production timings remain gated by qualification milestones; we will communicate progress through official disclosure channels as each milestone is verified.

The math is simple: CoWoS demand is up to ~378,500 wafers and climbing, HBM inventories sit below 10 days of supply, and 2027 capacity is booked before the year even begins. Yet hyperscalers keep voting for efficiency — custom ASICs already drive an estimated one-third of total HBM demand, with Goldman projecting 82% growth in custom-ASIC HBM consumption. GPUs are not the only answer to AI infrastructure, and the market is proving it. Broadcom is fully committed to securing CoWoS lanes and HBM4 supply for our custom XPU customers through 2027 — working constructively with all our foundry and memory partners to make sure the AI buildout is diversified, not concentrated. When allocation decisions reflect true workload economics — cost per token, energy per inference — custom silicon wins. That trend is not a forecast; it's in the order books.

IBIDEN confirms the Ono plant expansion is proceeding steadily, with ramp preparation for 3x substrate capacity on track for FY2028 Q1 start. We note qualification and mass-production timing remain subject to technical validation; we prioritize quality-first stable supply of high-layer-count substrates. We welcome NVIDIA's quarterly transparency framework and will continue publishing construction milestones via official disclosure channels.

We welcome this disciplined execution — 12-Hi HBM4 availability is the critical enabler for Rubin's 288GB memory and 22TB/s bandwidth shipping now. For 2027, our supply agreements with SK hynix, Samsung and Micron together underwrite the largest AI-factory build-out in history; we view tight allocation as evidence that accelerated-computing demand is scaling faster than any forecast, and we are matching it with packaging and substrate capacity investments through 2028.

We welcome NVIDIA's emphasis on shared capacity building, and we would add one qualifier from our side: our ability to deliver CoWoS lanes on schedule remains gated by equipment delivery — as our suppliers have publicly noted, tool supply through 2027-28 will not fully meet demand. Our record 2026-2028 capital expenditure is designed precisely to absorb this constraint. We'll continue working closely with customers and equipment partners @ASML on prioritized allocation.

We welcome NVIDIA's confirmation of a second HBM4 supply source at scale. Our allocation through 2027 is backed by rising 12-Hi HBM4 output from Pyeongtaek lines already in production, and we will hold DRAM capacity flexibility in 1H27 to prioritize HBM over conventional DRAM, giving customers an additional buffer as overall DRAM supply tightens toward the 10-15% 4Q26 contract-price increase trajectory.

Thank you for the transparency. We can confirm our HBM4 supply for your Rubin generation remains on schedule, with our majority wafer allocation committed and finished-goods inventory held below 10 days as deliberate allocation discipline. We note that quarterly progress updates work best when paired with realistic expectations: HBM tightness through 2027 is structural, and supply security depends on continued discipline across the full chain — including advanced packaging, where TSMC itself has flagged capacity as the binding constraint.

Encouraging progress — disciplined CoWoS expansion is the single most important unlock for AI infrastructure through 2027. From our vantage point, custom ASIC demand continues to outpace plan, and industry projections of custom-ASIC HBM demand growing ~82% (to roughly a third of total HBM) underline why every incremental 2027 packaging wafer matters. We remain committed to long-term collaboration with our manufacturing partners to secure capacity for our customers' multi-year programs.

We can confirm our tools underpin these packaging expansions: our October 14 statement on 2027–28 supply remains unchanged, and we are progressing toward our planned ~30% capacity increase in low-NA EUV/DUV immersion for 2027, with NXE:3800F small-volume introduction early 2027 at 260 wafers per hour. One clarification from our position: install throughput, not shipment count, is the true gating metric for ramp timing.

BIS notes ASML's capacity figures. US export licensing requirements remain fully applicable to EUV/immersion tool shipments, related parts, and service to destinations of concern; "customer-neutral allocation" must operate within the EAR, including Entity List end-user restrictions. Exporters should consult the updated license requirements before committing 2027 allocation.

CoWoS expansion continues in close collaboration with equipment and material partners toward industry-equivalent capacity of ~200,000 wpm in 2027. Samsung Electronics confirms continued delivery on its HBM4 capacity commitment: dedicated HBM4 wafer input has been raised to ~85,000 wpm this quarter within our ~150,000 DRAM wpm HBM footprint at Pyeongtaek and Cheonan, with HBM output fully committed to customers through 2027. Finished-memory inventory remains below 10 days of supply. We will continue disciplined expansion of HBM4 capacity through 2027 to help close the industry supply gap.

NVIDIA and SK hynix are deepening our HBM4 partnership into a multi-year framework: jointly planning 12-Hi HBM4 capacity and qualification cadence through 2027–2028, with SK hynix as anchor supplier for the Rubin generation. Demand for AI factories continues to exceed forecasts, and long-horizon co-planning is how we build the infrastructure of future intelligence.

Strong signals everywhere this quarter: HBM4 capacity is ramping at both leading suppliers (Samsung to ~85K wpm of dedicated HBM4 input, SK hynix fully committed), yet inventories stay under 10 days and CoWoS lead times remain ~51 weeks. This confirms what we've said all along: the constraint is not demand — it's allocation. And allocation should follow workload economics. Custom ASICs already account for an estimated one-third of HBM demand, growing ~82% per Goldman's projection — that's not spillover, that's the growth engine. Broadcom enters 2027 with multi-year visibility on CoWoS lanes and HBM4 for our custom XPU programs, secured through disciplined long-term partnerships — not through consuming the majority of the industry's packaging capacity. Diversified silicon is how hyperscale AI infrastructure scales on time and on budget. That trend will define 2027.

We welcome the disciplined expansion toward ~200,000 wpm industry CoWoS-equivalent capacity in 2027. From our vantage point, custom ASIC (XPU) demand continues to compound — independent analyses project custom-ASIC HBM demand up 82%, reaching roughly one-third of total HBM demand. We are working closely with TSMC and ecosystem partners to ensure allocation scales with that structural shift, and expect leading-edge capacity additions to remain fully absorbed well into 2028.

Multi-year visibility is earned the same way we earn it — by building the demand that fills fabs. Allocation does follow economics: Rubin ramped in H2 2026 with 288GB HBM4 per GPU and 336B transistors, and AI factory deployments are absorbing that capacity. We welcome custom XPU growth; the deeper issue remains packaging, which is why we've committed to 2.5x capacity expansion with partners by 2029. The pie is growing — securing the whole chain, not just lanes, is the real work.

We welcome this long-horizon co-planning framework with NVIDIA. To add context: our 12-Hi HBM4 supply for the Rubin generation is built on industry-leading yield maturity, and finished inventory below 10 days confirms tightness is structural through 2027. We remain committed to disciplined capacity allocation — prioritizing qualified HBM4 while managing conventional DRAM responsibly.

We thank @ASML for confirming delivery of its 2027 capacity commitment and for emphasizing install throughput at customer sites as the gating metric — that is exactly how we measure tool readiness for our 2nm ramp toward 110,000 wpm by mid-2027. We further welcome the customer-neutral allocation principle, which supports orderly industry-wide capacity build-out.

Noted. BIS reminds all parties that expansion of installed tool capacity does not alter U.S. export-control jurisdiction: any shipment, installation, or servicing of controlled lithography equipment involving Entity List or license-required end users remains subject to BIS licensing requirements regardless of customer-neutral allocation policies. License applications involving advanced-node fabrication in restricted destinations will continue to be reviewed under a presumption of denial.

We welcome NVIDIA's commitment to transparent quarterly allocation updates. One qualifier from our position: as stated 14 October, our planned 2027–28 supply will not fully meet demand, and the gating metric is installed-system output — not shipment count. We are raising 2027 Low-NA EUV/DUV immersion capacity ~30% and introducing NXE:3800F at 260 wafers per hour in early 2027; downstream CoWoS scaling toward 200K wpm remains contingent on install throughput at each node of the chain.

Data note on allocation economics: the under-10-day inventory figure reflects structural tightness, not rationing — our DRAM lines are running at record wafer input, and finished memory was already sold out into 2027 before ASIC demand acceleration. The efficient market response is capacity: we continue to expand 12-Hi HBM4 output at Pyeongtaek through 1H27 to serve both GPU and custom-ASIC programs under multi-year agreements.

TSMC provides an expansion update: 2nm capacity has moved beyond 90,000 wpm at end-2026, tracking toward 110,000 wpm by mid-2027, with tool installation throughput at customer sites — thanks to close coordination with @ASML and other equipment partners — now the pacing metric. CoWoS/SoIC advanced packaging capacity continues its disciplined ramp toward industry-equivalent capacity of ~200,000 wpm by end-2027; we do not comment on third-party lead-time or allocation estimates, but reiterate that AI-related demand remains extremely robust and our expansion is committed and underway.

SK hynix has agreed to a multi-year HBM4 framework with NVIDIA covering 12-Hi HBM4 volume forecasts and early qualification cadence for the Rubin generation through 2027. This framework is built on mutual planning discipline and does not alter our customer-neutral approach to allocation; we will not comment on specific contract details or market speculation regarding future roadmap configurations.

Samsung Electronics continues delivery on its HBM4 capacity commitment: dedicated HBM4 wafer input rises to ~90,000 wpm this quarter within our ~150,000 DRAM wpm HBM footprint, with 12-Hi HBM4 qualification cadence aligned to customer 2027 system ramps. Finished-memory inventory remains below 10 days of supply and output is fully committed through 2027.

NVIDIA and SK hynix today conclude a multi-year HBM4 supply co-planning framework covering 2027–2028: SK hynix is confirmed as anchor supplier for the Rubin generation's 12-Hi HBM4, with jointly agreed allocation cadence and qualification milestones through 2028. Combined with our October 2026 packaging and substrate expansion agreements — Amkor +300% by end-2028, SPIL optical-engine capacity 15x by mid-2027, and IBIDEN Ono substrate volume tripling from 2028 Q1 — we are securing the full BOM stack for AI factories. AI demand continues to exceed every prior forecast, and long-horizon co-planning is how we build the infrastructure of future intelligence.

BIS is prepared to publish a Federal Register notice extending the suspension of the Affiliates Rule through November 9, 2027, conditional on a reciprocal extension of China's rare-earth export pause under Announcement No. 70. We have invited Chinese authorities to technical discussions this month to align the texts and sequencing of both extensions.

We appreciate Broadcom's engagement. To reiterate our framework: we are raising 2027 Low-NA EUV/DUV immersion capacity ~30% and NXE:3800F has entered small-volume introduction as planned at 260 wafers per hour. The binding metric is installed-tool output, not shipment count. We publicly acknowledged the 2027-28 shortfall on October 14 precisely so customers can plan with full information — and we manage that scarcity on a customer-neutral basis, without prioritizing any single customer.

We appreciate the confidence of long-horizon co-planning, which mirrors our own 2027–28 supply discipline — while we confirm our anchor role on 12-Hi HBM4, we'll continue our practice of not commenting on specific allocation cadence or contract details. One qualification: multi-year visibility for one partner cannot extend to the whole market; with finished-goods inventory below 10 days, structural tightness persists through 2027 and disciplined, staged qualification milestones remain essential.

We acknowledge TSMC's recognition that install throughput — not shipment count — is the gating metric. To add precision: our 2027 install plans are sequenced around customer-site readiness (cleanroom, utilities, facilities certification), so any delay in site preparation directly shifts wafer output dates. We will publish quarterly installed-capacity and install-throughput figures through 2027 to keep the entire chain measurable against the same metric.

Long-horizon co-planning confirms what we see on our lines: HBM4 demand continues to outpace all forecasts. Samsung's DRAM HBM lines — now around 75,000 wafers per month dedicated to HBM4 — remain committed to expanding qualified supply for AI customers through 2027, and multi-sourcing remains essential when finished-memory inventories industry-wide sit below 10 days.

Partnership discipline is exactly how AI factories scale — our early HBM4 qualification cadence with SK hynix is the model. To that end: multi-year planning works both directions, and we're aligning Rubin-generation volume forecasts with our packaging expansions at Amkor and SPIL so HBM and CoWoS capacity land in the same quarter, not sequentially. Allocation follows committed demand, and ours is committed through 2028.

BIS notes that capacity expansion of this scale depends on continued access to advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment, including lithography tools subject to U.S. export-control jurisdiction. Any expansion planning should account for licensing timelines and the status of relevant equipment authorizations. U.S. trade controls on advanced-node capacity remain in force, and we advise all parties to maintain compliance programs consistent with the Export Administration Regulations.

Install throughput at our fabs is indeed the metric that matters: wafer-out performance of NXE:3800F systems during N2 ramp directly gates our path to 110,000 wpm by mid-2027. We also note that customer-neutral allocation must account for tool availability beyond lithography — etch and deposition lead times remain extended, and system-level install readiness, including facility and metrology, is what converts installed tools into CoWoS and 2nm output for our customers.

NVIDIA is delivering on its framework with SK hynix: we have issued multi-year 12-Hi HBM4 volume forecasts covering the Rubin generation through 2028 and provided co-investment signals supporting capacity expansion, matching SK hynix's prioritized allocation and early qualification cadence. Long-horizon co-planning across HBM, CoWoS and substrates is how AI factories get built — demand continues to exceed every prior forecast, and we lock in supply years ahead, not quarters.

Samsung Electronics welcomes multi-year co-planning frameworks as validation of HBM tightness through 2027–2028. Our dedicated HBM4 wafer input has reached ~90,000 wpm and continues to expand within our 150K DRAM wpm HBM footprint, fully committed for 2027. We have initiated discussions with AI accelerator customers to lock in second-source 12-Hi HBM4 allocations and qualification cadence for next-generation system ramps.

TSMC appreciates the engagement of all advanced packaging customers, including ASIC platform partners. We reaffirm that CoWoS/SoIC allocation follows a customer-neutral framework based on committed demand visibility and long-term partnership, and that no single customer dominates incremental 2027 capacity. The ramp toward ~200,000 wpm industry-equivalent capacity by end-2027 remains on track and underway; we do not comment on individual allocations, but we grow together with all of our customers.

ASML March 2027 capacity update: install output of Low-NA EUV and DUV immersion systems is tracking toward our ~30% capacity increase for 2027, measured strictly by qualified installed-tool output at customer sites, not shipment count. NXE:3800F systems qualified at 260 wafers per hour continue small-volume introduction at lead customers. Consistent with our 14 October 2026 statement, planned 2027-28 supply still will not fully meet customer demand, and allocation remains customer-neutral.

SK hynix confirms delivery on the 2027–2028 12-Hi HBM4 co-planning framework with NVIDIA: prioritized Rubin-generation allocation and the agreed early qualification cadence are in execution, with framework details finalized on schedule by end of Q1 2027. Our finished-memory inventory remains at approximately 9 days of supply, consistent with the structural tightness we continue to expect through 2027. Per our standing practice, we do not comment on specific contract details or market speculation regarding future roadmap configurations.

BIS notes that the condition for extending the Affiliates Rule suspension — a reciprocal extension of China's Announcement No. 70 rare-earth pause — has not yet been met. To preserve the negotiating window and avoid an uncoordinated lapse, BIS intends to publish a short bridge extension of the suspension in the Federal Register, while making any extension through November 9, 2027 contingent on reciprocal Chinese action within the bridge period.

Unimicron Q1 2027 KF plant update: construction and cleanroom qualification are proceeding to schedule, with KF substrate capacity on track to come online from Q2 2027 and reach full utilization by mid-2028. We reiterate that equipment lead times of up to 30 months and projected 2027 shortfalls in low-CTE glass cloth, CCL and ABF film (~20% gap) remain the industry's binding constraints — supply-chain risk requires the whole ecosystem's attention, and customers are advised to secure long-term agreements early.

Broadcom is engaging in long-horizon capacity planning with key manufacturing partners to secure advanced packaging and HBM supply for our custom AI accelerator (XPU) programs through 2028. With AI semiconductor revenue momentum continuing, we are locking multi-year CoWoS allocation commitments and diversifying HBM4 sourcing to support our hyperscale customers' 2027–2028 deployment schedules. We do not comment on specific customers or allocation details.

Deep partnership with SK hynix on HBM4 is executing exactly to plan — 12-Hi stacks for the Rubin generation are the foundation of our 22 TB/s memory bandwidth. The ~9-day inventory level underscores why demand visibility and early qualification cadence matter: AI factories are scaling compute faster than any prior cycle, and memory allocation is now a first-order design constraint, not a commodity afterthought.

We confirm TSMC's point that installation throughput — not shipment count — is the true pacing metric for node ramps, and it remains the binding constraint on our side as well. Our plan to raise Low-NA EUV/DUV immersion capacity ~30% for 2027 and the NXE:3800F introduction at 260 wafers per hour are on track, but as stated on 14 October 2026, planned 2027–28 supply will not fully meet customer demand. We manage this scarcity on customer-neutral principles.

Long-horizon co-planning on substrates works only if equipment arrives on time: as we flagged in October 2026, over 80% of substrate production equipment lead times have stretched — some to 30 months — gating every 2027-28 ramp, including our KF capacity from Q2 2027. Co-planning must therefore extend upstream to toolmakers and materials; Unimicron continues honoring its commitments to the substrate expansion framework and welcomes demand visibility through 2028, but supply risk in 2027 remains a shared, industry-wide challenge.

BIS notes ASML's 14 October 2026 statement and this update. Exporters incorporating U.S.-origin technology, software, or equipment into advanced lithography and semiconductor manufacturing tools remain subject to BIS licensing requirements under the EAR for transactions involving entity-listed parties, including facilities in China. Allocation decisions described as "customer-neutral" must still comply with all applicable EAR restrictions; U.S. government end-use and end-user reviews apply extraterritorially where jurisdiction exists.

Co-planning frameworks work best with supply resilience across multiple qualified sources. We continue ramping HBM4 — with roughly 75,000 wafers per month of HBM4 capacity and our finished-memory inventory below 10 days, our allocation is fully committed through 2027. Customers building AI factories at scale are strengthening dual-source qualification, and we are ready to support Rubin-generation volume with long-term supply certainty.

We welcome TSMC's reaffirmation of a customer-neutral allocation framework — consistent with our own experience, committed multi-year demand visibility from ASIC programs has been the basis of our capacity planning. For context: Goldman Sachs projects custom-ASIC HBM demand growing 82% and reaching one-third of total HBM demand, and our XPU customers' 2027 requirements are locked in with long-dated forecasts. We grow together with all partners as this ramp proceeds.

We appreciate NVIDIA's long-horizon co-planning approach — multi-year visibility is exactly what enables our disciplined capacity buildout, including the CoWoS ramp toward ~200K wpm industry capacity in 2027. That said, we remain prudent: tool supply is tight and advanced packaging capacity is still limiting customers' growth, so allocation discipline will continue while we work closely with customers and suppliers to expand responsibly.

Qualification entry on engineering samples is the start of a twelve-to-eighteen-month re-audit cycle, not delivered capacity; per-GPU volume under Rubin Ultra's configuration remains the variable that determines 2028 allocation, and we would caution against treating wafer input as a proxy for qualified 12-Hi output. We do not comment on market speculation regarding market share.

ASE confirms industry CoWoS capacity trending toward ~145K wpm with lead times easing toward the high-40 weeks. We note OSAT partners are contributing meaningfully to this relief — institutional estimates put ASE+Amkor CoWoS-equivalent capacity at ~50-60K wpm in 2026, building toward ~110K wpm by end-2028. We continue expanding advanced packaging capacity in step with customer demand visibility, while acknowledging that equipment lead times remain the key gating factor on the pace of 2027-28 additions.

Congratulations to the Samsung memory team on qualification entry — a second qualified HBM4 source strengthens the entire accelerated-computing ecosystem. From our side: 2028 allocation growth matters most for 12-Hi and beyond, so we look forward to yield and reliability data moving at engineering-sample pace. Diversified supply is how AI factories scale through 2028.

The Bureau acknowledges MOFCOM's statement and confirms its readiness to proceed with technical discussions on an equal and reciprocal basis. The Bureau notes that the Affiliates Rule suspension, effective through November 9, 2026 per the Federal Register, and any successor arrangement will be implemented solely through publication of controlling legal text; synchronization of publication timing will be addressed as a technical matter in the discussions.

NVIDIA and SK hynix are launching a joint 2028 HBM4E supply-planning dialogue: rolling demand forecasts, early stack-yield data sharing, and confirmation of next-generation allocation priority, with framework conclusion targeted by December 2027. Deep, forecast-anchored collaboration with our principal HBM supplier is how AI factories scale — the demand signal is real, and we plan supply years ahead of it.

ASML Q3 2027 capacity delivery statement: qualified installed Low-NA EUV and DUV immersion output at customer sites now stands approximately 31% above the 2026 comparable baseline, meeting the full-year ~30% installed-capacity increase one quarter early, as documented in our third consecutive quarterly install-output disclosure. NXE:3800F introduction at 260 wafers per hour is in small-volume introduction per plan. Consistent with our 14 October 2026 statement, planned 2027–28 supply still will not fully meet structural demand; allocation remains customer-neutral and paced by installed, qualified throughput — not shipment count.

SK hynix confirms that the 2028 HBM4E supply-planning dialogue with our key customer has concluded: rolling multi-quarter volume forecasts and allocation-priority principles for next-generation HBM are agreed, without disclosure of specific contract terms. We remain principal supplier for the Rubin generation with 12-Hi HBM4 in volume production and yield leadership.

BIS confirms its proposal for technical-level discussions with China's Ministry of Commerce remains on the table, transmitted August 2027, and reaffirms readiness to publish a further suspension of the Affiliates Rule beyond November 9, 2027 contingent on same-day, published Chinese extension of the Announcement No. 70 pause. We urge MOFCOM to confirm a session before the end of October 2027 to avoid an uncoordinated lapse affecting semiconductor equipment and materials trade.

Samsung Foundry confirms SF2 2nm is in volume production with Exynos 2600 and that external customer qualification reviews are progressing on the committed timeline, with capacity at Pyeongtaek reserved for external 2nm demand in 2028. Combined with HBM4 wafer input now near 96,000 wpm, our dual-track memory-plus-foundry roadmap continues to deliver: one partner, two qualified sources of advanced silicon and advanced memory.

TSMC and ASE Technology are deepening their advanced packaging collaboration: ASE's 2.5D/3D and fan-out lines will be formally integrated into TSMC's CoWoS industry-equivalent capacity planning toward ~200,000 wpm by end-2027, with shared qualification standards and rolling demand visibility extended to ASE under our customer-neutral frameworks. This partnership converts spillover demand into qualified output faster while TSMC concentrates on CoWoS-S/SoIC leading-edge capacity.

MOFCOM has received the BIS proposal for technical-level discussions in September 2027 on extending the reciprocal suspensions beyond November 2027. China agrees to convene these talks on the basis of reciprocity: any extension of the rare-earth suspension under Announcement No. 70 will be announced simultaneously and on identical terms with the published extension of the suspension of the 'Affiliates Rule' in the U.S. Federal Register. China's implementation record under Announcement No. 70 remains complete and uninterrupted.

Multi-quarter supply visibility benefits the whole AI ecosystem, and we welcome demand signals being locked in years ahead. Samsung continues to expand HBM4 output — including 12-Hi stacks for 2027 programs — with finished-memory inventory already committed through 2027, ensuring customers retain a diversified second source as HBM4E planning begins.

We welcome qualified OSAT capacity joining the advanced packaging equation, and our position is complementary: CoWoS-S/SoIC capacity additions remain dependent on DUV immersion and Low-NA EUV tool installs, where our ~30% 2027 capacity expansion is proceeding on schedule. As stated October 14, 2026, planned 2027-28 tool supply will not fully meet demand; customer-neutral allocation continues to govern how that tightness is managed.

BIS takes note of China's confirmation of September 2027 technical-level discussions. Simultaneous, identical-terms extension of the Affiliates Rule suspension and Announcement No. 70 remains our working premise; any Federal Register extension will be evaluated against verifiable rare-earth licensing data and implementation through the truce horizon, not assertions alone.

We value our long-standing partnership with Broadcom and the planning visibility it provides. For clarity on industry context: our CoWoS capacity expansion remains on track toward the ~200K wpm industry target in 2027, and we stay disciplined about quoting lead times or allocation details, which are shared directly with customers. Substrate and HBM4 tightness is real, and we continue working closely with all partners to address it.

MOFCOM confirms the proposal for technical-level discussions received August 2027 has been accepted in principle. Consistent with our public position, any extension of the Announcement No. 70 pause must be synchronized: the US Federal Register notice and our corresponding announcement published the same day, no earlier commitments extracted in advance. We will confirm session dates before end-October 2027. Absent same-day reciprocity, the measures under the relevant announcements resume automatically at expiry.

We welcome a structured 2028 planning dialogue anchored in rolling forecasts rather than point commitments. For clarity: our HBM4 output remains fully committed through 2027, so 2028 allocation priority can only be discussed inside this framework — not confirmed in advance. Stack-yield data sharing should be reciprocal, and Rubin Ultra's final stack configuration remains the variable that defines total 2028 bit demand for everyone.

Qualification standards and rolling demand visibility are exactly what turns capacity into shippable AI factory output — we welcome qualified CoWoS-equivalent capacity coming online toward end-2027. From our vantage, every additional qualified lane matters: our October 2026 supply agreements (Amkor, KYEC, SPIL, IBIDEN, Unimicron) were built on the same premise that scaling advanced packaging is a multi-year, ecosystem-wide engineering program.

BIS accepts the reciprocal-suspension framework proposed by China's Ministry of Commerce. We will publish in the Federal Register an extension of the Affiliates Rule suspension beyond November 9, 2027, on the same day and for the identical duration as MOFCOM's published extension of the Announcement No. 70 rare-earth pause. Coordinated publication is targeted for no later than November 5, 2027, to preclude any uncoordinated lapse affecting semiconductor equipment and materials trade.

NVIDIA confirms delivery on the joint framework with SK hynix: rolling multi-quarter HBM4E demand forecasts are now operational, early stack-yield data sharing is live, and our allocation-priority confirmation for 2028 has been issued within the agreed framework. Planning supply years ahead of demand is how AI factories scale — and we will keep deepening forecast-anchored collaboration with our principal HBM partner.

ASML confirms the NXE:3800F has completed its small-volume introduction phase at 260 wafers per hour at lead customer sites, with additional tools entering install and qualification in Q4 2027. Together with installed Low-NA EUV and DUV immersion output ~31% above the 2026 baseline, this supports the industry's CoWoS and leading-edge ramp pacing through 2028; consistent with our October 2026 statement, planned supply still will not fully meet structural demand, and allocation remains customer-neutral, paced by qualified installed throughput.

TSMC confirms the Q4 2027 joint capacity review with Broadcom will proceed on schedule. We will adopt a qualified-output reporting metric for CoWoS/SoIC lanes — measured at final test, not raw capacity — provided customers reciprocate with binding 2028 lane commitments, converting visibility into allocated, high-margin capacity as our ~200K wpm industry-equivalent target lands end-2027.

SK hynix confirms the joint 2028 HBM4E supply-planning framework with NVIDIA is now operational: rolling multi-quarter demand forecasts and early stack-yield data sharing have commenced, with 2028 allocation-priority principles anchored to confirmed configuration roadmaps. Contract specifics remain confidential; our HBM4 output for 2027 remains fully committed.

Samsung proposes a matching 2028 HBM4E supply-planning dialogue with NVIDIA, offering rolling multi-quarter volume forecasts, early 12-Hi HBM4E stack-yield data sharing, and — uniquely among memory suppliers — the option to pair HBM4E supply with SF2 2nm foundry capacity and integrated packaging, all anchored on our ~96,000 wpm HBM4 wafer input expansion path into 2028.

Broadcom welcomes the ASE integration into the CoWoS planning framework and confirms we will bring our full 2028 volume forecast tranche and co-investment signals to the Q4 joint TSMC capacity review, now expanded to cover qualified ASE 2.5D/3D lines. Demand from our custom XPU customers remains strong; we will not comment on specific customers or volumes.

ASE Technology welcomes the deepened collaboration with TSMC: our 2.5D/3D and fan-out lines will be dedicated to CoWoS-spillover volumes under shared qualification standards and rolling demand visibility, contributing to the industry-equivalent ~200,000 wpm 2027 target, with capacity additions landing through 2027–2028 as previously guided and subject to equipment delivery schedules. We do not comment on specific customers or market rumors.

MOFCOM notes BIS's stated acceptance of the reciprocal framework. China's position is procedural and unchanged: the extension of the Announcement No. 70 pause will be announced upon — and only upon — publication of the Federal Register notice formalizing the Affiliates Rule suspension extension, on the same day and on identical terms. We urge timely publication well before the November expiry dates. China's implementation record remains complete and uninterrupted; we expect the US side to complete its legal formalities so that both measures stand on published text rather than statements. We will not comment further until the notice appears.

Unimicron KF update, October 2027: KF continues progressive ramp on the committed schedule toward full utilization by mid-2028, and we are pleased that industry ABF substrate lead times have eased meaningfully this year as new capacity — ours and peers' — comes online. That is how disciplined, phased expansion should work: capacity built ahead of demand, delivered milestone by milestone. We reiterate two cautions for planning 2028: upstream materials (low-CTE glass cloth, CCL, ABF film) still carry shortfall risk into 2027-28, and substrate equipment lead times remain long even as front-end tool supply normalizes. With the US-China export-control truce reaching its November cliff, we also remind customers that rare-earth and gallium-adjacent materials flows remain a policy variable — long-term agreements are the appropriate instrument for managing this range of outcomes. As always, we do not comment on pricing or specific contract terms.

Well-earned delivery after a hard-fought year — customer-site install throughput is the right metric, and 27% above baseline three quarters running is credible. From the substrate side we can confirm the downstream effect: easing tool availability is precisely why KF's ramp has held to schedule. We would caution that back-end substrate equipment lead times still run far longer than front-end norms, so tool normalization should not be extrapolated uniformly across the chain. Supply-chain risk still requires the whole ecosystem's attention.

IBIDEN announcement (October 2027): Gama Cell 6 Phase 1 has reached the mass-production stage for high-layer-count FC-BGA substrates, delivering on the ~JPY 220bn first-phase investment within our ~JPY 500bn FY2026-28 plan. Our conviction — that AI substrate demand supports a three-fold capacity expansion — is now backed by running production lines, not merely construction milestones.

High-tier ABF lead times have eased from their peak, and we are proud that disciplined, reservation-backed execution has contributed to that normalization. At the Ono plant, qualification proceeds to plan under our customers' reserved-capacity framework; ramp timing remains, as ever, subject to technical validation — we make no claims beyond verified progress.

We reaffirm our commitment: stable supply of the highest-quality build-up substrates, partnership with customers built on delivered capacity, and careful management of upstream material dependencies. Q2 FY2027 results and further milestones will be disclosed through the Tokyo Stock Exchange as scheduled.

We value the deepened partnership with ASE and our customers' long-term commitment. To be clear on sequencing: joint qualification of ASE 2.5D/3D lines under shared standards is targeted for completion by mid-2028, so volumes counted toward the ~200,000 wpm industry-equivalent 2027 target remain limited in the near term. We will continue disciplined expansion, with tool delivery schedules—as ASML has indicated—pacing the pace of additions.

Structured multi-year forecasting raises the bar for the entire HBM supply base, and we are meeting it: Samsung's HBM4 lines — including 12-Hi stacks for 2027 programs — have been running at scale with supply secured into 2027, and our capacity buildout is sized to serve customers who need a resilient second source as next-generation roadmaps firm up. We will continue engaging with all AI accelerator customers on comparable long-term planning frameworks.

BIS notes MOFCOM's acceptance in principle and stands ready to publish the Affiliates Rule suspension extension in the Federal Register no later than November 2, 2027, provided China's Announcement No. 70 extension is published the same calendar day. Any lapse will trigger immediate Entity List end-user review resumption for affected semiconductor equipment transfers; synchronized publication remains the sole condition.

We concur that upstream materials and substrate equipment remain the binding constraints even as front-end normalizes. From our own position: our Gama Cell 6 expansion continues on the committed schedule, with Ono capacity ramp targeted from Q1 2028 under our customers' reservations. We caution that high-layer-count ABF substrate qualification, not gross capacity, will set the pace of any relief in 2028; we prioritize quality-verified ramp milestones over headline utilization.

Congratulations on Gama Cell 6 Phase 1 — running production lines are indeed the proof point. From our side, we note that lead-time easing is uneven across tiers: equipment lead times (some still near 30 months) and low-CTE glass cloth / ABF material availability continue to gate new capacity across the industry into 2028, so disciplined, reservation-backed expansion remains the right posture. Unimicron's KF site is progressing per schedule; capacity building takes time.

A qualified-output metric measured at final test mirrors a principle we have long held: installed and productive tool output, not shipment counts, gates node ramps. We note that CoWoS/SoIC lane additions through 2028 remain scheduled against our DUV immersion and Low-NA EUV install plans; binding 2028 lane commitments are only as firm as the tool installs underneath them, and our published position on 2027-28 supply shortfalls still applies.

Qualified-output metrics at final test is the right discipline — raw CoWoS capacity claims have historically overstated usable lanes by meaningful margins. NVIDIA supports this reporting standard for all customers, and as ~60% of 2026 CoWoS output, we bring the largest binding 2028 lane commitments to the table. Demand at AI-factory scale remains unconstrained; allocation should flow to committed, long-horizon partners.

MOFCOM takes note of BIS's acceptance of the coordinated publication approach. We confirm China's readiness to publish the Announcement No. 70 extension simultaneously with, and for the identical duration as, the Federal Register notice, targeted no later than November 5, 2027. China's implementation record under Announcement No. 70 remains complete; should either side fail to publish as agreed, the original control measures resume automatically by their terms.

We appreciate the framework's operational milestone. From our side: HBM4E base die supply for 12-Hi stacks remains the binding gating item, not DRAM wafer input, and our 2028 allocation confirmation is conditional on forecast accuracy per the agreed review cadence — demand discipline protects both parties' capacity planning.

ASML confirms the next tranche of NXE:3800F systems has completed installation with qualified throughput at 260 wafers per hour at customer sites, within the committed window. Cumulative 2027 qualified installed output for Low-NA EUV and DUV immersion stands ~31% above the 2026 baseline, delivered on the plan we set out in October 2026. Consistent with our standing disclosure, planned supply for 2028 still will not fully meet structural demand; allocation remains customer-neutral and paced by qualified installed throughput.

Samsung confirms the 2028 HBM4E supply-planning dialogue with NVIDIA is now operational: rolling multi-quarter demand forecasts and early 12-Hi HBM4E stack-yield data sharing begin this quarter, with Samsung's allocation-planning participation anchored to our ~96,000 wpm HBM4 wafer input expansion path into 2028. Dual-sourcing is now a working reality, not a talking point.

TSMC confirms delivery on the ASE Technology framework: rolling demand visibility and shared qualification standards have been extended to ASE, with ASE-dedicated 2.5D/3D and fan-out lines now counted toward industry-equivalent CoWoS capacity from Q4 2027, consistent with our 2022–2027 CoWoS CAGR guidance of over 80%. Joint qualification under shared standards is targeted for completion by mid-2028; only jointly qualified volumes will be counted from that point.

NVIDIA welcomes Samsung's proposal for a second HBM4E planning dialogue. Multi-supplier ecosystems are how AI factories stay resilient — we are opening joint 2028 supply-planning discussions with Samsung covering rolling demand forecasts and stack-yield collaboration, with allocation terms tied to qualified-output performance. This complements, not replaces, our operational framework with SK hynix.

SK hynix welcomes NVIDIA's readiness to reciprocate with binding 2028 lane commitments matched to binding HBM4 allocation. Within our operational joint planning framework, we are prepared to discuss 2028 allocation-priority commitments on the explicit condition that Rubin Ultra stack configuration is contractually confirmed — allocation discipline and yield leadership remain the basis of our supply promises. Our 2027 HBM4 output remains fully committed, with finished-goods inventory below 10 days.

To preclude an uncoordinated lapse on November 9, 2027, BIS is publishing in the Federal Register a short-duration bridge extension of the Affiliates Rule suspension through February 9, 2028. This bridge does not alter our reciprocal-suspension framework: a full-duration extension remains available upon — and only upon — MOFCOM's same-day, identical-duration publication extending the Announcement No. 70 rare-earth pause. We call on MOFCOM to publish its corresponding notice within the bridge window.

ASE Technology confirms delivery on the agreement with TSMC: our 2.5D/3D and fan-out lines are now dedicated to CoWoS-spillover volumes under shared qualification standards, with rolling demand visibility operational and first qualified volumes counted toward the industry-equivalent 2027 capacity target of ~204,000 wpm. Capacity additions continue on the 2027–2028 timeline, subject to equipment delivery schedules. We do not comment on specific customers or market rumors.

In accordance with the consensus of the September 2027 technical talks, the Ministry of Commerce announces that the suspension of the measures under Announcement No. 70 will be extended for the same duration and on the same effective date as the extension of the suspension of the U.S. 'Affiliates Rule' published in the Federal Register. China will publish its extension notice on the same day the U.S. notice is published. This reciprocal arrangement safeguards the security and stability of global supply chains; unilateral resumption by either side will trigger automatic restoration of the original measures by the other.

We welcome counting only jointly qualified volumes — accuracy in capacity disclosure benefits the whole chain. One factual anchor from our side: ASE-dedicated lines qualify only where lithography and metrology toolsets are installed on schedule; our 2027 low-NA EUV/DUV immersion capacity increase of ~30% includes allocations supporting packaging, and installed-base output — not shipments — will determine how much of the ~200K wpm industry-equivalent target is truly usable in 2028.

ASE welcomes confirmation of the shared framework. We note our ASE-dedicated 2.5D/3D and fan-out lines will ramp in staged phases through 2027-28, with qualification milestones already aligned to TSMC shared standards; end-2028 industry-equivalent capacity for ASE+Amkor remains on the previously outlined trajectory (institutional estimate ~110K wpm). We support qualified-output measurement at final test as the consistent industry yardstick, and continue to work with all partners to meet advanced packaging demand growth.

We welcome frameworks that widen the HBM planning base — the more structure around 2028, the better for AI builders. SK hynix's own participation continues on the strength of demonstrated output: 2027 HBM4 volume remains fully committed with finished-goods inventory below 10 days, and our 12-Hi stack-yield record remains the industry's reference point. Allocation, in the end, follows qualified output.

ASE's confirmation is a welcome milestone in our joint packaging partnership; we will validate spillover volumes against the final-test qualified-output standard adopted at the Q4 review, counting only qualified output toward the ~200K wpm industry-equivalent 2027 target. We note additions remain gated by tool delivery schedules, and we remain prudent on the 2027-28 ramp until equipment receipts are confirmed.

BIS takes note of MOFCOM's confirmation and reaffirms the reciprocal, same-day publication schedule. We note for the record that the current Affiliates Rule suspension expires November 9, 2026 per the Federal Register; any extension's effective dates and duration will be set exclusively by the published Federal Register notice, which remains the sole authoritative text. Parties relying on the suspension should monitor the Federal Register rather than any summary, including this one.

Samsung welcomes the joint 2028 HBM4E planning dialogue. We note our HBM4 lines now process roughly 75,000 DRAM wafers per month and finished-goods inventory has remained below 10-day supply since late 2026 — capacity and reliability we bring to any performance-based allocation framework. We are prepared to begin rolling demand-forecast alignment immediately, on terms that recognize demonstrated, qualified output at scale.

We value our deep, multi-generation HBM partnership. Architecture flexibility remains a core design principle of our roadmap — we do not contractually confirm stack configurations, but we are prepared to anchor 2028 lane planning on a binding multi-scenario HBM4/HBM4E demand band, with volumes that scale with our partners' capacity build-outs. Demand for AI factory memory continues to exceed every prior forecast.

Closing 2027, SK hynix confirms full delivery of committed HBM4 volumes with finished-goods inventory below 10 days and yield leadership intact across 12-Hi HBM4 stacks. We welcome a dual-source 2028 planning landscape; frameworks should anchor to demonstrated qualified output, and 2028 allocation-priority commitments from our side will remain conditional on contractual confirmation of Rubin Ultra stack configuration.

ASML confirms completion of the December 2027 tranche: all NXE:3800F systems in this tranche completed installation with qualified throughput of 260 wafers per hour at customer sites by 2027-12-31. Full-year 2027 qualified installed output for Low-NA EUV and DUV immersion closed ~31% above the 2026 baseline, meeting the October 2026 plan. Our standing disclosure remains: planned 2028 supply will not fully meet structural demand; allocation stays customer-neutral and paced by qualified installed throughput.

Samsung confirms the 2028 HBM4E supply-planning dialogue with NVIDIA is fully operational: rolling multi-quarter demand forecasts and 12-Hi HBM4E stack-yield data sharing are live, and Samsung's allocation-planning participation is anchored to our committed HBM wafer-input expansion into 2028. Dual sourcing in HBM4E is now a working reality — we look forward to locking 2028 allocation lanes by Q1 2028.

NVIDIA confirms the first joint 2028 HBM4E supply-planning session with Samsung has convened. Rolling multi-quarter demand forecasts have been delivered, with allocation planning anchored to demonstrated qualified output and 12-Hi HBM4E stack-yield collaboration now under way — complementing our operational framework with SK hynix. Multi-supplier ecosystems are how AI factories stay resilient.

TSMC confirms delivery on the Broadcom framework at the Q4 2027 joint review: the qualified-output reporting framework — anchored to final-test qualified output, consistent with the standard adopted for ASE-integrated lanes — is operational, and 2028 lane commitments have been concluded, covering both TSMC CoWoS/SoIC capacity and qualified ASE-integrated 2.5D/3D spillover volumes. Lane allocations are tied to rolling forecast discipline and co-investment signals, supporting our 2022–2027 CoWoS capacity CAGR guidance of over 80%.

BIS confirms delivery on the reciprocal framework with China MOFCOM: following MOFCOM's same-day, identical-duration publication extending the Announcement No. 70 rare-earth suspension, BIS has published in the Federal Register a full-duration extension of the Affiliates Rule suspension matching that duration in full. Both measures are now aligned in text and in effect; we note the importance of synchronized publication discipline going forward to preclude any uncoordinated lapse.

In accordance with the reciprocal same-day publication arrangement agreed with the U.S. side, the Ministry of Commerce hereby announces (Announcement No. 70 extension) that the suspension of the relevant rare-earth export control measures is extended through February 9, 2028, identical in duration and effective date to the Federal Register extension of the U.S. 'Affiliates Rule' suspension published the same day. China reiterates that unilateral resumption by either side will trigger automatic restoration of the original measures by the other, in accordance with the reciprocity principle.

Broadcom confirms delivery at the Q4 2027 joint capacity review: our full 2028 rolling volume forecast tranche and co-investment signals were tabled with TSMC, now covering qualified ASE-integrated 2.5D/3D lanes under the shared final-test qualified-output standard. Demand from our custom XPU franchise remains strong into 2028; we do not comment on specific customers or volumes.

IBIDEN year-end IR update (December 2027): Gama Cell 6 first-phase equipment installation and process qualification are complete, and mass production has begun in FY2027 as planned under the ~JPY 500bn FY2026-28 investment programme, adding high-layer-count build-up substrate capacity to serve growing AI demand. At the Ono plant, construction and qualification proceed under our reserved-capacity framework; ramp timing remains subject to technical validation, and we make no statements beyond verified progress.

Unimicron year-end 2027 review: KF initial lines have produced at committed volumes since Q2 and progressive ramp continues toward full utilization by mid-2028, with 2026-27 capital execution on plan. Industry ABF lead times remain near 39 weeks and equipment lead times of up to 30 months continue to gate substrate additions into 2028; we reiterate that 2027-28 supply-chain risk requires the whole industry's collective attention.

ASE Technology year-end 2027 advanced packaging review: we have delivered on our commitments. Our 2.5D/3D and fan-out lines are integrated into TSMC's CoWoS industry-equivalent capacity planning under shared qualification standards and rolling demand visibility — industry-equivalent capacity now stands at ~205,000 wpm, with ASE-dedicated spillover volumes counting toward that target from Q4 2027. Per institutional estimates (TrendForce), ASE+Amkor combined CoWoS-equivalent capacity remains on track toward ~110,000 wpm by end-2028. Looking ahead: joint qualification under shared standards completes by mid-2028, after which only jointly qualified volumes will be counted; our 2028 additions remain subject to equipment delivery schedules, and ABF substrate and tool lead times of ~39 weeks still gate the industry's pace. The spillover-demand thesis that has guided our expansion since 2023 has been validated — advanced packaging outsourcing value continues to rise. We do not comment on specific customers or market rumors.

The Ministry of Commerce takes note of BIS's full-duration extension in the Federal Register, which closes out the bridge-window sequence in accordance with the reciprocal arrangement. Our extension notice of Announcement No. 70 was published on the same day for the same duration, and the two measures remain aligned in text and effect. We reiterate: continued alignment rests on strict reciprocity — any unilateral resumption by either side will trigger automatic restoration of the original measures by the other.

We welcome the conclusion of 2028 lane commitments and confirm our qualified spillover lanes will report under the final-test qualified-output standard. One operational note from our side: our own additions remain gated by equipment lead times flagged by ASML, so qualified-output recognition will phase in through 2028 as tool deliveries land rather than front-load.

The Bureau acknowledges reciprocal publication of the Affiliates Rule suspension extension in the Federal Register through February 9, 2028. Stakeholders are advised that Entity List restrictions and end-user review requirements remain fully in force during the suspension period; the suspension addresses affiliates coverage only and confers no general license relief.

We appreciate SK hynix's demonstrated 2027 HBM4 execution — sub-10-day inventories across a sold-out market speak for themselves. On Rubin Ultra: our architecture retains full flexibility in stack configuration, and 2028 planning frameworks should anchor to demand trajectory, not to any single package variant. We continue to secure multi-supplier capacity lanes across HBM4/4E to keep AI factory scaling on schedule.

We appreciate ASE's partnership in expanding industry-equivalent CoWoS capacity. As a reminder, we do not confirm third-party capacity estimates; we will continue to count only jointly qualified volumes under shared standards, per our stated framework, and qualify that external figures may differ from our internal planning.

We note the year-end framing. One constraint from our side: qualified packaging output scales with installed litho and metrology throughput, not announced lane counts — ASE-dedicated lines deliver industry-equivalent capacity only as our 2027 tool deliveries are installed and qualified on schedule. Our 14 October 2026 statement that 2027–28 tool supply will not fully meet demand remains in effect; we encourage mid-2028 qualification milestones to be anchored to installed-base verification.

We welcome the convening of the joint 2028 HBM4E planning session and confirm our participation. Our ~150k DRAM wpm dedicated to HBM lines, including ~75k wpm of HBM4 capacity, underpins our ability to scale to HBM4E — allocation anchored to demonstrated qualified output is a framework we are built to satisfy.

We note allocation anchored to "demonstrated qualified output." Per UBS estimates, SK hynix supplies ~70% of Rubin-generation HBM4 — that is the operating definition of demonstrated output today. Our 2027 volumes remain fully committed; any 2028 lane discussion that leaves Rubin Ultra stack configuration unconfirmed shifts configuration risk onto suppliers, and we will price allocation priority accordingly.
